hypothesis: Deterministic wide-tile selection for long prefill: when min(Sq, Skv) >= 8192, skip the autotuner and launch _attn_fwd directly with the 128x128 w8 s2 config (BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, num_warps=8, num_stages=2). Shorter prefills keep the existing 9-config autotuner unchanged. The kernel body, pre-pass, grid order and decode path are unchanged.
rationale: results.tsv shows the prefill_8192/16384 timings are bimodal ever since exp 34 added 128x128 s2. Before exp 34 (128x64 only), 8k was always >= 1.865 ms and 16k always >= 7.64 ms. After it, runs land either at ~1.83/7.38-7.43 ms (exps 35, 36, 40, 43; exp 43 changed only decode, so its prefill speedup comes purely from config choice) or at the old ~1.87/7.66 ms (HEAD's kept run, exps 37, 39). 32k is stable at ~29.7 (it always picks 128x128). So 128x128 is ~2% faster at 8k and ~3.5% faster at 16k, but the per-run autotuner, timing on a first call, picks 128x64 about half the time. The kept best_score run was a slow-mode run on both rows. This is a shape-keyed config choice (a general length threshold where diagonal waste is small relative to per-tile overheads), not a per-shape constant: below 8192 the tuner still decides because there is no clear signal at 4096 and 2048 picks 128x64. It also removes the tuning cost and the selection variance that has made several earlier prefill experiments look like wins or losses on noise.
expected_effect: prefill_8192 to about 1.83-1.84 ms and prefill_16384 to about 7.38-7.43 ms on every run (both 2-3.5% faster than HEAD's recorded run). prefill_32768 is unchanged (~29.7, same config). prefill_2048/4096 and all decode rows are unchanged. That gives a geomean gain of about +0.5%, and lower run-to-run variance.
